newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC cuts propylene output due to overstock.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC cuts propylene output due to overstock.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it was reducing propylene production at its Kaohsiung refinery by ten percent due to reduce stocks.
"Chinese Petroleum is cutting production on propylene in order to reduce inventory," an official told Reuters.
Officials expected the reduction to be temporary, and said its Kaohsiung refineries would resume normal operation within two weeks.
Chinese Petroleum's Kaohsiung refinery complex includes its third, fourth, and fifth refining units that can produce a total of 220,000 tonnes of propylene a year, official said.
The Kaohsiung complex' first refining unit was demolished in 1990 and second was closed in April 1994.
Chinese Petroleum had planned to move its second refining unit to Indonesia, but later canceled its plan due to site selection problems.
